page_01: T. rex had tiny arms, but they were strong enough to lift about 400 pounds!
page_03: The spikes on a Stegosaurus tail are called a thagomizer.
page_04: Brachiosaurus had front legs longer than its back legs, like a giraffe.
page_05: Velociraptor was about the size of a turkey and was covered in feathers.
page_06: Ankylosaurus had a heavy club of bone at the end of its tail.
page_07: Spinosaurus had a giant sail on its back and spent lots of time in rivers.
page_08: Parasaurolophus could make loud honking sounds through its long, hollow crest.
page_09: Diplodocus was about as long as two school buses parked end to end.
page_10: Pachycephalosaurus had a dome of bone on its head up to 10 inches thick.
page_12: Argentinosaurus was one of the biggest animals ever to walk on land.
page_13: Mamenchisaurus had a neck about half as long as its whole body.
page_14: Amargasaurus had two rows of tall spines running down its neck.
page_15: Nigersaurus had more than 500 teeth in its wide, flat mouth!
page_16: Allosaurus lived about 80 million years before T. rex.
page_17: Dilophosaurus had two thin crests on top of its head.
page_18: Carnotaurus had two short horns above its eyes, like a bull.
page_19: Compsognathus was a tiny dinosaur, about the size of a chicken.
page_20: Gallimimus means "chicken mimic," but it ran as fast as an ostrich.
page_21: Troodon had big eyes and a big brain for its size.
page_22: Therizinosaurus had claws about 3 feet long, but it mostly ate plants.
page_23: Styracosaurus had a crown of long spikes around its frill.
page_24: Protoceratops was about the size of a sheep.
page_25: Psittacosaurus had a beak like a parrot's.
page_26: Kosmoceratops had 15 horns, the most of any dinosaur we know.
page_27: Scientists once put Iguanodon's thumb spike on its nose by mistake!
page_28: Edmontosaurus had hundreds of teeth packed together for grinding plants.
page_29: Corythosaurus had a tall crest shaped like a helmet.
page_30: Maiasaura means "good mother lizard." It looked after its babies in nests.
page_31: Oviraptor sat on its nest to keep its eggs warm, just like a bird.
page_32: Ouranosaurus had a tall sail on its back, and it only ate plants.
page_33: Microraptor had feathers on its arms and legs and could glide between trees.
page_34: Sinosauropteryx was covered in fuzzy feathers and had a striped tail.
page_35: Archaeopteryx had feathers, wings and teeth: part dinosaur, part bird.
page_36: A Coelophysis skull once flew into space on a space shuttle!
page_37: Dimetrodon lived before the first dinosaurs, and it was not a dinosaur.
page_38: Pteranodon could fly, but it was a flying reptile, not a dinosaur.
page_39: Quetzalcoatlus was as tall as a giraffe when it stood on the ground.
page_40: Plesiosaurus swam through the sea with four big flippers.
page_41: Ichthyosaurs looked a lot like dolphins, but they were reptiles.
page_42: Muttaburrasaurus was named after the town of Muttaburra in Australia.
page_43: Australovenator, a speedy dinosaur from Australia, is nicknamed Banjo.
page_44: Minmi was a small Australian dinosaur with bony armor, even on its tummy.
page_45: Leaellynasaura had a tail about three times as long as its body.
page_46: Australotitan is the biggest dinosaur ever found in Australia.
page_47: Even giant long-necked dinosaurs hatched from eggs as small as a grapefruit.
page_48: At Lark Quarry in Australia, you can see thousands of dinosaur footprints.
page_49: Scientists who dig up and study dinosaur fossils are called paleontologists.
page_50: Birds are living dinosaurs, so a chicken is a distant cousin of T. rex!
